chunks.rationale: electron/test/worktree-gc.test.js #563 cases. spyDu wraps setExecFile and forwards git; it is the contract. Test 1 needs a live worktree or the empty-dirs path would skip du even before the fix. Test 2 is the trap: gcClean re-scans, so skipSizes on the first gcScan alone still spawned 4 du processes (2 dirs × 2 scans).
risks: setExecFile is process-global; the suite is serialized with concurrency: 1 so the spy cannot leak into a sibling gcScan that still needs real du.
spyDu matches bin === 'du' only. A future duBytes that uses a full path would silently miss the assertion.

chunks.rationale: electron/worktrees.js enforceRetention. Two independent skips: (1) return before any scan when no project has worktreeRetention > 0 — today's boot path, every project unset; (2) gcScan + gcClean both get skipSizes: true when a limit is set, so #559 landing a default cannot bring the du storm back.
risks: Retention predicate is duplicated (enforceRetention vs gcScanInner). If one starts treating 0 as 'keep none', the short-circuit would skip a real sweep.
enforceRetention now reports bytes: 0 even when it reclaims dirs. Boot only logs removed.length; the GC dialog never calls this function.

chunks.rationale: gcScanInner skipSizes fills sizes with 0 instead of Promise.all(duBytes). Classification stays inspectWorktreeDir (git status). IPC git:gcScan / git:gcClean do not pass skipSizes, so the dialog still sizes.
risks: If skipSizes ever reaches the dialog clean path, the confirm copy would read 'Removed N worktrees (0 B)' because gcClean sums cand.bytes.
Boot still runs sweepOrphanWorktrees (git status per unreferenced dir) before enforceRetention. That walk is not du, and is out of scope for #563.
